title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：tax　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 tax 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the clerk ① paid the tax that no applicant in the office would have counted, and he said the paying was the whole of the month. The ② tax, meaning the charge itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed uncounted in the book; a tax, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ tax in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ tax at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A tax, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the clerk said the counting is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the tax was the whole of the matter, meaning the duty and not the charge. The ⑥ tax, meaning the duty and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; tax, he said, is either something you pay or the only word that means both a charge and a duty. He said the duty is the part they remember.

By 1984 the ⑦ tax had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ tax of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of counting; tax, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ tax I remember is the charge counted in the file, which closed in 1986 and is still counted as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ tax, my mother said in 1988, is the only charge that improves by being counted; every tax, she said, is a duty that has agreed to look like a charge. She said the duty was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 税（指办事处里每一笔旁边的那一笔）
B. n. 税（指那笔税本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：pay the tax 缴这一笔税
D. n. 税（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 税之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的税之事）
F. n. 税（指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一笔）
G. n. 税、义务（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 义务（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: paid the tax that no applicant in the office would have counted
The tax, meaning the charge itself and not the stamp
the tax at the far counter
the tax was the whole of the matter
the tax had become a line in a file
The tax of the whole thing
A tax, my mother said in 1988

answers.why: pay the tax 意为“缴这一笔税”，1979 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯清点的一笔税做了一遍。
tax 意为“税”，指那笔税本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被清点。
tax 意为“税”，指办事处里每一笔旁边的那一笔，每一笔旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
tax 意为“税”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
tax 意为“税、义务”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这笔义务就是那件事的全部。
tax 意为“义务”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那笔税，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
tax 意为“税”，指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一笔，到 1984 年这一笔成了卷宗里的一行。
tax 意为“税之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的税之事是一处办事处和三个月份的清点。
tax 意为“税”，我记得的是卷宗里清点过的那一笔，1986 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一笔。
tax 为抽象总称，母亲 1988 年说，税是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的税。
